cases.expected: Iterator instance is not null and hasNext() returns false for an empty Zone
cases.description: Create a new Zone with no RRsets. Call zone.iterator() and verify that the returned Iterator<RRset> is non‑null and that iterator.hasNext() == false.

cases.expected: Iterator returns the single RRset added to the Zone and then reports no further elements
cases.description: Create a Zone, add one RRset (e.g., using zone.addRRset(rrset)). Obtain an iterator via zone.iterator(). The first call to iterator.next() must return the same RRset instance, iterator.hasNext() must be false afterwards, and a subsequent call to next() must throw NoSuchElementException.

cases.expected: Iterator traverses all RRsets in the order defined by ZoneIterator (insertion order for this test) and then reports no further elements
cases.description: Create a Zone and add three distinct RRsets (rrset1, rrset2, rrset3). Call zone.iterator() and collect the results of successive next() calls. The collected list should be [rrset1, rrset2, rrset3] and after the third element iterator.hasNext() must be false. A fourth next() call must throw NoSuchElementException.

cases.expected: Two iterators obtained from the same Zone operate independently but start from the same initial state
cases.description: Create a Zone, add two RRsets. Obtain iteratorA = zone.iterator() and iteratorB = zone.iterator(). Advance iteratorA once (iteratorA.next()). iteratorB must still return the first RRset on its next() call, showing that each iterator has its own cursor.

cases.expected: Calling next() on an empty iterator throws NoSuchElementException
cases.description: Create an empty Zone. Obtain iterator = zone.iterator(). Directly call iterator.next() without checking hasNext(). The call must throw java.util.NoSuchElementException.

cases.expected: Calling remove() on the iterator throws UnsupportedOperationException (or IllegalStateException if remove is supported only after next)
cases.description: Create a Zone, add at least one RRset, obtain iterator = zone.iterator(). Without calling next(), invoke iterator.remove(). The expected behavior is that the iterator throws java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException (or IllegalStateException if the implementation follows the standard contract).

cases.expected: Iterator does not reflect RRsets added to the Zone after the iterator was created; it only iterates over the RRsets that existed at creation time.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add RRsetA, obtain iterator = zone.iterator(), then add RRsetB to the Zone. Verify that iterator.hasNext() is true, iterator.next() returns RRsetA, and subsequent iterator.hasNext() is false (RRsetB is not seen).

cases.expected: Iterator continues to return RRsets that were present at creation even if they are removed from the Zone after iterator creation.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add RRsetA and RRsetB, obtain iterator = zone.iterator(), then remove RRsetB from the Zone via zone.removeRRset(...). Verify that iterator.next() returns RRsetA, then iterator.next() returns RRsetB, and iterator.hasNext() is false, showing that removal after iterator creation does not affect the iterator.

cases.expected: Multiple calls to hasNext() before calling next() do not advance the iterator and always return the same result.
cases.description: Create a Zone with two RRsets (rrset1, rrset2). Obtain iterator = zone.iterator(). Call iterator.hasNext() three times consecutively; each call should return true. Then call iterator.next() and verify it returns rrset1. Subsequent hasNext() calls behave normally.

cases.expected: Calling hasNext() after the iterator is exhausted repeatedly returns false without throwing.
cases.description: Create a Zone with a single RRset. Obtain iterator, call iterator.next() to consume the element, then call iterator.hasNext() multiple times; each call should return false.

cases.expected: Calling remove() after a successful next() throws UnsupportedOperationException.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add one RRset, obtain iterator = zone.iterator(), call iterator.next() to retrieve the element, then invoke iterator.remove(). The call must throw java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException.

cases.expected: Enhanced for‑loop iterates over all RRsets in the order defined by ZoneIterator (which follows the internal map's ordering).
cases.description: Create a Zone and add three RRsets with distinct names that sort lexicographically as rrsetA, rrsetB, rrsetC. Use a for‑each loop (`for (RRset r : zone)`) to collect the visited RRsets into a list. Verify that the collected list equals [rrsetA, rrsetB, rrsetC] and that the loop terminates after the third element.

group: Zone.iterator() handling of duplicate names with different types

cases.expected: Iterator returns separate RRset instances for the same name but different record types, preserving both entries.
cases.description: Create a Zone, add two RRsets that share the same Name (e.g., "example.com.") but have different types (A and AAAA). Obtain iterator and collect results. Verify that both RRsets appear in the iteration (order may follow internal map ordering).
